English: But the Jews who were in Susa assembled together on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth days of the month; and on the fifteenth day of that month, they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

tcz: Hijeh chun, tuni changei’in thinglhanga um Judate kho gamla a umhon hiche nikholeh, phalbi kichai kon lamleh kumlhun golvah abollun akipah khomun nehle chah thilpeh ho akithot to jiuvin ahi.
en: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, a holiday, and a day of sending presents of food to one another.
text:
EST 9:19
Thadou: Hijeh chun, tuni changei’in thinglhanga um Judate kho gamla a umhon hiche nikholeh, phalbi kichai kon lamleh kumlhun golvah abollun akipah khomun nehle chah thilpeh ho akithot to jiuvin ahi.
English: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, a holiday, and a day of sending presents of food to one another.

tcz: Mordecai in hiche thilsoh hohi ajih lut’in Xerxes gamsung jousea anai ahin agamla a um ahin Judate hohi lekha anathot jin ahi.
en: Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of the King Ahasuerus, both near and far,
text:
EST 9:20
Thadou: Mordecai in hiche thilsoh hohi ajih lut’in Xerxes gamsung jousea anai ahin agamla a um ahin Judate hohi lekha anathot jin ahi.
English: Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of the King Ahasuerus, both near and far,

tcz: Hiche nini sung hi kumseh a golvah abolji diuvin ana sei peh tan ahi.
en: to enjoin them that they should keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month Adar yearly,
text:
EST 9:21
Thadou: Hiche nini sung hi kumseh a golvah abolji diuvin ana sei peh tan ahi.
English: to enjoin them that they should keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month Adar yearly,

tcz: Ama hiche nikho sunga hi kipana golvah bolding leh nehle chah kipehto a, gentheite manbeiya pehding in ana seipeh in ahi. Hiche hin Judate agalmi teuva konna kipana amunao, alunggim naova konna thanopna amunao ageldoh jing nadiu ahi.
en: as the days in which the Jews had rest from their enemies, and the month which was turned to them from sorrow to gladness, and from mourning into a holiday; that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, and of sending presents of food to one another, and gifts to the needy.
text:
EST 9:22
Thadou: Ama hiche nikho sunga hi kipana golvah bolding leh nehle chah kipehto a, gentheite manbeiya pehding in ana seipeh in ahi. Hiche hin Judate agalmi teuva konna kipana amunao, alunggim naova konna thanopna amunao ageldoh jing nadiu ahi.
English: as the days in which the Jews had rest from their enemies, and the month which was turned to them from sorrow to gladness, and from mourning into a holiday; that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, and of sending presents of food to one another, and gifts to the needy.

tcz: Hiti chun Judaten Mordecai thilgon hohi anop peh un, hiche hi kumseh in achepi tauvin ahi.
en: The Jews accepted the custom that they had begun, as Mordecai had written to them,
text:
EST 9:23
Thadou: Hiti chun Judaten Mordecai thilgon hohi anop peh un, hiche hi kumseh in achepi tauvin ahi.
English: The Jews accepted the custom that they had begun, as Mordecai had written to them,

tcz: Judate galmi Agagi mi Hammedatha chapa Haman chun Judate tehi suhmang helna dinga nikhokhat lhendohna dinga vangvetna ananei ahi. (Hiche avangvetna chu Purim akiti)
en: because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast “Pur”, that is the lot, to consume them and to destroy them;

tcz: Ahinlah lengnu Estherhi lengpa anga ahunglut phat in, aman dan chomkhat ahin sem’in hichun Haman tohgon phaloutah chu amachunga achuhlo tan ahi. Haman le achate chu mol lhon hemjet chunga akhailih ataove.
en: but when this became known to the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked plan, which he had planned against the Jews, should return on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
text:
EST 9:25
Thadou: Ahinlah lengnu Estherhi lengpa anga ahunglut phat in, aman dan chomkhat ahin sem’in hichun Haman tohgon phaloutah chu amachunga achuhlo tan ahi. Haman le achate chu mol lhon hemjet chunga akhailih ataove.
English: but when this became known to the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked plan, which he had planned against the Jews, should return on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

tcz: Hijeh’a chu hiche golnop nahi Purim kiti ahi, ajehchu hiche hi gollui paova vangvetna ktina ahi. Amaho tah in anathoh khahsao ahijeh leh Mordecai in anajihlut ahijeh'in ahin chepi taove.
en: Therefore they called these days “Purim”, from the word “Pur.” Therefore because of all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and that which had come to them,
text:
EST 9:26
Thadou: Hijeh’a chu hiche golnop nahi Purim kiti ahi, ajehchu hiche hi gollui paova vangvetna ktina ahi. Amaho tah in anathoh khahsao ahijeh leh Mordecai in anajihlut ahijeh'in ahin chepi taove.
English: Therefore they called these days “Purim”, from the word “Pur.” Therefore because of all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and that which had come to them,

tcz: Gamjousea Judate ten hiche chon nahi chepi dingin anom’un chuleh achilhahte jousen jong ajui diuvin ana kilol’un ahi. Amahon hiche nikho teni hi kumseh leh akitepna nikho ahi alopna neijing dingin ana phongdoh un ahi.
en: the Jews established and imposed on themselves, on their descendants, and on all those who joined themselves to them, so that it should not fail that they would keep these two days according to what was written and according to its appointed time every year;

tcz: Hiche nikho ho chu lenggam sunga khopi hole gambih ho jousea insung jousen akhang akhanga ageldoh jinguva anit jing diu ahi. Hiche Purim golvah ankong hi Judate lah a itih hijongleh mangthah louva anit jing ding chuleh ipi thil anasoh ham tihi akhang akhanga mansah louhel ding ahi.
en: and that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor their memory perish from their offspring.
text:
EST 9:28
Thadou: Hiche nikho ho chu lenggam sunga khopi hole gambih ho jousea insung jousen akhang akhanga ageldoh jinguva anit jing diu ahi. Hiche Purim golvah ankong hi Judate lah a itih hijongleh mangthah louva anit jing ding chuleh ipi thil anasoh ham tihi akhang akhanga mansah louhel ding ahi.
English: and that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor their memory perish from their offspring.

tcz: Abihail chanu lengnu Esther le Judate mi Mordecai in lekha khat anajih lhonin, masangjep a Mordecai in ana sutsa Purim kiman di thudol se se chu, lengnun thanei tah namdetna anei tan ahi.
en: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.
text:
EST 9:29
Thadou: Abihail chanu lengnu Esther le Judate mi Mordecai in lekha khat anajih lhonin, masangjep a Mordecai in ana sutsa Purim kiman di thudol se se chu, lengnun thanei tah namdetna anei tan ahi.
English: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.

tcz: Hiche lekha chu Judate jouse anathot un chule Xerxes lenggam a gambih jakhat le somni le sagi sungah ana thot soh hel un ahi. Lekhathot a chu Judate lah a chamna le lungmon na leng hen akitin ahi.
en: He sent letters to all the Jews in the hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus with words of peace and truth,
text:
EST 9:30
Thadou: Hiche lekha chu Judate jouse anathot un chule Xerxes lenggam a gambih jakhat le somni le sagi sungah ana thot soh hel un ahi. Lekhathot a chu Judate lah a chamna le lungmon na leng hen akitin ahi.
English: He sent letters to all the Jews in the hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus with words of peace and truth,

tcz: Judate mi Mordecai leh lengnu Esther in dan a anatundoh lhon Purim golvah hi anikho kipeh dungjuija kumseh a nit dinga ana kiphutdoh ahi. (Mipite hin amaho dingleh achilhah ho diuva anngol naleh lunghemna anathoh khom banguva hiche Purim golvah jonghi ana tundoh u ahi).
en: to confirm these days of Purim in their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had decreed, and as they had imposed upon themselves and their descendants in the matter of the fastings and their mourning.
text:
EST 9:31
Thadou: Judate mi Mordecai leh lengnu Esther in dan a anatundoh lhon Purim golvah hi anikho kipeh dungjuija kumseh a nit dinga ana kiphutdoh ahi. (Mipite hin amaho dingleh achilhah ho diuva anngol naleh lunghemna anathoh khom banguva hiche Purim golvah jonghi ana tundoh u ahi).
English: to confirm these days of Purim in their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had decreed, and as they had imposed upon themselves and their descendants in the matter of the fastings and their mourning.

tcz: Hitia hi Purim chon nahi Esther thupeh in namdetna anei hetjing dingin lekhajol khat’a kijih lut tai.
en: The commandment of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.
text:
EST 9:32
Thadou: Hitia hi Purim chon nahi Esther thupeh in namdetna anei hetjing dingin lekhajol khat’a kijih lut tai.
English: The commandment of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.

tcz: Xerxes lengpa hin ama gamsung pumpi keo hilouva twikhanglen pang mun gamlatah a jong kai analah ahi.
en: King Ahasuerus laid a tribute on the land and on the islands of the sea.
text:
EST 10:1
Thadou: Xerxes lengpa hin ama gamsung pumpi keo hilouva twikhanglen pang mun gamlatah a jong kai analah ahi.
English: King Ahasuerus laid a tribute on the land and on the islands of the sea.

tcz: Ama tohdoh thupitah tah hole, aman ana tunlet Mordecai nasatna hohi Media le Persia lengte thusimbu’a kijihlut’a ahi.
en: Aren’t all the acts of his power and of his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai, to which the king advanced him, written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
text:
EST 10:2
Thadou: Ama tohdoh thupitah tah hole, aman ana tunlet Mordecai nasatna hohi Media le Persia lengte thusimbu’a kijihlut’a ahi.
English: Aren’t all the acts of his power and of his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai, to which the king advanced him, written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

tcz: Judate mi Mordecai hi Xerxes lengpa bantah a thanei in apangin ahi. Amahi Judate te lah a mithupitah ahung hin chuleh jana sangtah anapeuvin ahi, ajehchu aman amite dingin thilpha anatong jingin chuleh khang nunungho changeija aphatna diuvin thu anaseijin ahi.
en: For Mordecai the Jew was next to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews and accepted by the multitude of his brothers, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his descendants.
text:
EST 10:3
Thadou: Judate mi Mordecai hi Xerxes lengpa bantah a thanei in apangin ahi. Amahi Judate te lah a mithupitah ahung hin chuleh jana sangtah anapeuvin ahi, ajehchu aman amite dingin thilpha anatong jingin chuleh khang nunungho changeija aphatna diuvin thu anaseijin ahi.
English: For Mordecai the Jew was next to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews and accepted by the multitude of his brothers, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his descendants.

tcz: Phatkhat hin Uz gam sunga Job kiti mikhat ana cheng in, amapa chu nolnabei leh lungtheng sel ahi. Amapan Pathen aging in thilphalou jousea kona kikangse jinga um ahi.
en: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
text:
JOB 1:1
Thadou: Phatkhat hin Uz gam sunga Job kiti mikhat ana cheng in, amapa chu nolnabei leh lungtheng sel ahi. Amapan Pathen aging in thilphalou jousea kona kikangse jinga um ahi.
English: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.

tcz: Joh hin chapa sagi le chanu thum aneiye.
en: There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.
text:
JOB 1:2
Thadou: Joh hin chapa sagi le chanu thum aneiye.
English: There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.

tcz: Chule Job hin kelngoi sang sagi, sangongsao sang thum, bongchal kop janga, le sanganpi janga aneiye. Amapa hin soh jong tamtah anei ahi. Atahbeh in Job hi hiche gamkai sungse dinga ahaopen ahi.
en: His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.
text:
JOB 1:3
Thadou: Chule Job hin kelngoi sang sagi, sangongsao sang thum, bongchal kop janga, le sanganpi janga aneiye. Amapa hin soh jong tamtah anei ahi. Atahbeh in Job hi hiche gamkai sungse dinga ahaopen ahi.
English: His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.

tcz: Job chapate aphat lhingpen pen chun ainnuva nehkhom donkhom abol tenguleh, asopiu numei thumho jong chu golvah bolkhompi din akou jiuve.
en: His sons went and held a feast in the house of each one on his birthday; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
text:
JOB 1:4
Thadou: Job chapate aphat lhingpen pen chun ainnuva nehkhom donkhom abol tenguleh, asopiu numei thumho jong chu golvah bolkhompi din akou jiuve.
English: His sons went and held a feast in the house of each one on his birthday; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

tcz: Hiche golvah chu akichai teng nikho phabep jouleh Job chun achate athenso jin ahi. Job chu jingkah matah in athou jin khat cheh a din govam thilto abolpeh ji'e. Ajeh chu Job in hiti hin aseijin, “Kachate hi ana chonseuvin tin chule alungthim uva jong Pathen agaosap sao himai theijinte,” ati. Hiti hin Job in abol jing jenge.
en: It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts.” Job did so continually.
text:
JOB 1:5
Thadou: Hiche golvah chu akichai teng nikho phabep jouleh Job chun achate athenso jin ahi. Job chu jingkah matah in athou jin khat cheh a din govam thilto abolpeh ji'e. Ajeh chu Job in hiti hin aseijin, “Kachate hi ana chonseuvin tin chule alungthim uva jong Pathen agaosap sao himai theijinte,” ati. Hiti hin Job in abol jing jenge.
English: It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts.” Job did so continually.

tcz: Nikhat hi van thutanna in na thutanho ama ho cham chamin Pakai masanga ahung kikhomun chule hehhatpa Satan chu amaho toh ahung lhung khome.
en: Now on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before the LORD, Satan also came among them.
text:
JOB 1:6
Thadou: Nikhat hi van thutanna in na thutanho ama ho cham chamin Pakai masanga ahung kikhomun chule hehhatpa Satan chu amaho toh ahung lhung khome.
English: Now on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before the LORD, Satan also came among them.

tcz: “Hoiya konna hung nahim?” tin Pakaiyin Satan adonge. Satan in Pakai adonbut in, Leiset chung kaga vet lhih lea, thilsoh jouse kaga vetle ahi.
en: The LORD said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”
text:
JOB 1:7
Thadou: “Hoiya konna hung nahim?” tin Pakaiyin Satan adonge. Satan in Pakai adonbut in, Leiset chung kaga vet lhih lea, thilsoh jouse kaga vetle ahi.
English: The LORD said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”

tcz: Chuin Pakaiyin Satan jah a, “Kalhachapa Job khu nahet em? Leiset a dinga miphapen ahi. Amahi nolnabei, milungthengsel ahin, aman Pathen aging in chule thilphalou jousea konin akikangsen ahi,” ati.
en: The LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant, Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil.”
text:
JOB 1:8
Thadou: Chuin Pakaiyin Satan jah a, “Kalhachapa Job khu nahet em? Leiset a dinga miphapen ahi. Amahi nolnabei, milungthengsel ahin, aman Pathen aging in chule thilphalou jousea konin akikangsen ahi,” ati.
English: The LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant, Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil.”

tcz: Satan in Pakai adonbut in, “Henge Job in Pathen aginna ajeh hoitah anei ahi.
en: Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
text:
JOB 1:9
Thadou: Satan in Pakai adonbut in, “Henge Job in Pathen aginna ajeh hoitah anei ahi.
English: Then Satan answered the LORD, and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?

tcz: Ama ahin ain ahin chule anei jouse kulpi kikai khum banga, akim vella pal banga naum chahkheh’a nangin atohna jousea nakhan tousah jeh’a bou ahi. Ven ichan geija haosa hitam?
en: Haven’t you made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
text:
JOB 1:10
Thadou: Ama ahin ain ahin chule anei jouse kulpi kikai khum banga, akim vella pal banga naum chahkheh’a nangin atohna jousea nakhan tousah jeh’a bou ahi. Ven ichan geija haosa hitam?
English: Haven’t you made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.

tcz: Nakhut lhangin lang anei jouse lahmang peh le chun; chuteng leh namai chang tah’a na gaosap jeng ding ahi,” ati.
en: But stretch out your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will renounce you to your face.”
text:
JOB 1:11
Thadou: Nakhut lhangin lang anei jouse lahmang peh le chun; chuteng leh namai chang tah’a na gaosap jeng ding ahi,” ati.
English: But stretch out your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will renounce you to your face.”

tcz: Pakaiyin Satan jah’a aseijin. “Aphai, amapa khu napatep thei ahi. Chule anei jouse chunga nabol nom chan nabol thei ahinai, atahsa vang suhset peh hih in,” ati. Chuin Satan in jong Pakai umna adalhatai.
en: The LORD said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power. Only on himself don’t stretch out your hand.” So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.
text:
JOB 1:12
Thadou: Pakaiyin Satan jah’a aseijin. “Aphai, amapa khu napatep thei ahi. Chule anei jouse chunga nabol nom chan nabol thei ahinai, atahsa vang suhset peh hih in,” ati. Chuin Satan in jong Pakai umna adalhatai.
English: The LORD said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power. Only on himself don’t stretch out your hand.” So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.

tcz: Nikhat Job achapate le achanuten aupa pen pao in’a an anehkhom adonkhom laitah un,
en: It fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
text:
JOB 1:13
Thadou: Nikhat Job achapate le achanuten aupa pen pao in’a an anehkhom adonkhom laitah un,
English: It fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,

tcz: Thupole khat in Job in'ah hiche thusoh hi ahinpoi; “Nabongchal hon lou akhoijuva, akimvella sangan hon an aneh laijun,
en: that a messenger came to Job, and said, “The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys feeding beside them,
text:
JOB 1:14
Thadou: Thupole khat in Job in'ah hiche thusoh hi ahinpoi; “Nabongchal hon lou akhoijuva, akimvella sangan hon an aneh laijun,
English: that a messenger came to Job, and said, “The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys feeding beside them,

tcz: Seba miten eihin bulhu tauvin, ganchaho jouse akiguh manguvin chule natong ho athat gamun, keima changseh hi nangma seipeh dia hung sohcha kahi,” ati.
en: and the Sabeans attacked, and took them away. Yes, they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
text:
JOB 1:15
Thadou: Seba miten eihin bulhu tauvin, ganchaho jouse akiguh manguvin chule natong ho athat gamun, keima changseh hi nangma seipeh dia hung sohcha kahi,” ati.
English: and the Sabeans attacked, and took them away. Yes, they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

tcz: Amapan hiche thuhi asei nalaijin thupole dang khat in hiche thusoh hi ahinpoi, “Vanna konin Pathen meikong ahung lhan kelngoite le achingho akavam gamtai; keima changseh hi nangma seipeh dinga hung sohcha kahi,” ati.
en: While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “The fire of God has fallen from the sky, and has burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
text:
JOB 1:16
Thadou: Amapan hiche thuhi asei nalaijin thupole dang khat in hiche thusoh hi ahinpoi, “Vanna konin Pathen meikong ahung lhan kelngoite le achingho akavam gamtai; keima changseh hi nangma seipeh dinga hung sohcha kahi,” ati.
English: While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “The fire of God has fallen from the sky, and has burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

tcz: Amapan hiche thuhi asei nalaijin, thupole athum channa pa ahung lhungin, hiche thusoh hi ahinpon, “Chaldea mite loithum jenin ahin delkhumun sangongsao jouse agumang un; chule nasaohte athatgam tauve, keima changseh hi nangma seipeh dinga hung sohcha kahi,” ati.
en: While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “The Chaldeans made three bands, and swept down on the camels, and have taken them away, yes, and killed the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”
text:
JOB 1:17
Thadou: Amapan hiche thuhi asei nalaijin, thupole athum channa pa ahung lhungin, hiche thusoh hi ahinpon, “Chaldea mite loithum jenin ahin delkhumun sangongsao jouse agumang un; chule nasaohte athatgam tauve, keima changseh hi nangma seipeh dinga hung sohcha kahi,” ati.
English: While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “The Chaldeans made three bands, and swept down on the camels, and have taken them away, yes, and killed the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

tcz: Hichepan thu asei nalaijin, thupole adang khat in hiche thusoh hi ahinpo paijin, “Nachapate le nachanu ten aupa pen pao in na anekhom adonkhomun ahileh,
en: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
text:
JOB 1:18
Thadou: Hichepan thu asei nalaijin, thupole adang khat in hiche thusoh hi ahinpo paijin, “Nachapate le nachanu ten aupa pen pao in na anekhom adonkhomun ahileh,
English: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,

tcz: Photlot chang in, gammang lah a konin huipi hattah khat in aumnau in chu aninglang jousea ahin nuh leh in chu ahung chimlhan nachate jouse athigam soh tauve. Keima changseh hi nang seipeh dinga hung sohcha kahi,” ati.
en: and behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and they are dead. I alone have escaped to tell you.”
text:
JOB 1:19
Thadou: Photlot chang in, gammang lah a konin huipi hattah khat in aumnau in chu aninglang jousea ahin nuh leh in chu ahung chimlhan nachate jouse athigam soh tauve. Keima changseh hi nang seipeh dinga hung sohcha kahi,” ati.
English: and behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and they are dead. I alone have escaped to tell you.”

tcz: Job adingdoh in thilsoh lunggim najeh in asangkhol chol chu abottel in, alu akivo chaijin, chule chibai boh din tolla akun lhatai.
en: Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
text:
JOB 1:20
Thadou: Job adingdoh in thilsoh lunggim najeh in asangkhol chol chu abottel in, alu akivo chaijin, chule chibai boh din tolla akun lhatai.
English: Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.

tcz: Aman, “Kanu naobua konna kasagoh keuva hungdoh kahin, chule kadalhah teng sagoh keu kahi ding ahi. Kanei jouse Pakaiyin eipeh ahin, chule Pakaiyin akilah mang ahi; Pakai min chu vahchoijin umhen,” ati.
en: He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the LORD’s name.”
text:
JOB 1:21
Thadou: Aman, “Kanu naobua konna kasagoh keuva hungdoh kahin, chule kadalhah teng sagoh keu kahi ding ahi. Kanei jouse Pakaiyin eipeh ahin, chule Pakaiyin akilah mang ahi; Pakai min chu vahchoijin umhen,” ati.
English: He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the LORD’s name.”

tcz: Hicheng jouse ahin Pathen themmo chansah nan achonsepoi.
en: In all this, Job didn’t sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.
text:
JOB 1:22
Thadou: Hicheng jouse ahin Pathen themmo chansah nan achonsepoi.
English: In all this, Job didn’t sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.

tcz: Nikhat van thutanna in na miho chu acham tah uvin Pakai masangah ahung kilah kit uvin, hiche a chun hehhatpa Satan chu amaho lah a ahung pange.
en: Again, on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before the LORD, Satan came also among them to present himself before the LORD.
text:
JOB 2:1
Thadou: Nikhat van thutanna in na miho chu acham tah uvin Pakai masangah ahung kilah kit uvin, hiche a chun hehhatpa Satan chu amaho lah a ahung pange.
English: Again, on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before the LORD, Satan came also among them to present himself before the LORD.

tcz: “Hoiya konna hung nahim?” tin Pakaiyin Satan adonge. Satan in Pakai chu adonbut in, “Keiman leiset kaga khollen; thilsoh jouse kaga velhan ahi” ati.
en: The LORD said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered the LORD, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”
text:
JOB 2:2
Thadou: “Hoiya konna hung nahim?” tin Pakaiyin Satan adonge. Satan in Pakai chu adonbut in, “Keiman leiset kaga khollen; thilsoh jouse kaga velhan ahi” ati.
English: The LORD said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered the LORD, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”

tcz: Hichun Pakaiyin Satan adongin, “Kasohpa Job khu namu tah em? Amahi leiset chunga dinga miphapen ahin, nolnabei, milung thengsel ahi, Pathen agingin thilse jouse a konna kikangse jing mi ahi, ajeh beija nangin amakhu chonset sah teidinga nagot vang'in tunjong lungtheng sellin aum jinge,” ati.
en: The LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”
text:
JOB 2:3
Thadou: Hichun Pakaiyin Satan adongin, “Kasohpa Job khu namu tah em? Amahi leiset chunga dinga miphapen ahin, nolnabei, milung thengsel ahi, Pathen agingin thilse jouse a konna kikangse jing mi ahi, ajeh beija nangin amakhu chonset sah teidinga nagot vang'in tunjong lungtheng sellin aum jinge,” ati.
English: The LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”

tcz: Satan in Pakai adonbut in “Vun dinga vun ahi, mihem khat in ahinkho ahuhdohna dinga anei agou jouse apeh doh teiding ahi.
en: Satan answered the LORD, and said, “Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.
text:
JOB 2:4
Thadou: Satan in Pakai adonbut in “Vun dinga vun ahi, mihem khat in ahinkho ahuhdohna dinga anei agou jouse apeh doh teiding ahi.
English: Satan answered the LORD, and said, “Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.

tcz: Ahin, nakhut lhangin lang adamtheina khu lahmang peh le chun namaichang laitaha nagaosap tei ding ahi!” ati.
en: But stretch out your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your face.”
text:
JOB 2:5
Thadou: Ahin, nakhut lhangin lang adamtheina khu lahmang peh le chun namaichang laitaha nagaosap tei ding ahi!” ati.
English: But stretch out your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your face.”

tcz: “Aphai, amapa chunga hin nalungdei tah boltan; ahin ahinkho vang khen peh in,” tin Pakaiyin Satan aseipeh e.
en: The LORD said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand. Only spare his life.”
text:
JOB 2:6
Thadou: “Aphai, amapa chunga hin nalungdei tah boltan; ahin ahinkho vang khen peh in,” tin Pakaiyin Satan aseipeh e.
English: The LORD said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand. Only spare his life.”

tcz: Hijeh chun Satan chun Pakai angsung adalhan, chule Job chu nat hoisetah uilut alujanga kipat akengto geijin a onglai beihellin aphah sahtai.
en: So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.
text:
JOB 2:7
Thadou: Hijeh chun Satan chun Pakai angsung adalhan, chule Job chu nat hoisetah uilut alujanga kipat akengto geijin a onglai beihellin aphah sahtai.
English: So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.

tcz: Job in atahsa vun chu bel hallin akhot in vut bollah a atouve.
en: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
text:
JOB 2:8
Thadou: Job in atahsa vun chu bel hallin akhot in vut bollah a atouve.
English: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.

tcz: “Tuchan geija lungtheng sella naum jing nahlai ding ham? Pathen chu gaosap in lang thijengin,” tin ajinun Job jah a chun aseije.
en: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die.”
text:
JOB 2:9
Thadou: “Tuchan geija lungtheng sella naum jing nahlai ding ham? Pathen chu gaosap in lang thijengin,” tin ajinun Job jah a chun aseije.
English: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die.”

tcz: Ahinlah Job in adonbut in, “Nangin numei ngol khat thusei bangin naseije, Pathen khutna konna chu einin thil pha jeng jeng ikisanna chule thilse kisan louva ium ding ham?” ati. Thilsoh hijat chunga jong hin Job in thilse aseipoi.
en: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job didn’t sin with his lips.
text:
JOB 2:10
Thadou: Ahinlah Job in adonbut in, “Nangin numei ngol khat thusei bangin naseije, Pathen khutna konna chu einin thil pha jeng jeng ikisanna chule thilse kisan louva ium ding ham?” ati. Thilsoh hijat chunga jong hin Job in thilse aseipoi.
English: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job didn’t sin with his lips.

tcz: Job agolte thum hon lungset umtah anat thohgim thu ajahdoh phat uvin ama ama in cheh a konin alhamon dingle alhembi dingin thakhat'in ahung kikhom uve. Amin hou chu Teman mi Eliphaz, Shuh mi Bildad chule Naamath mi Zophar ahiuve.
en: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.
text:
JOB 2:11
Thadou: Job agolte thum hon lungset umtah anat thohgim thu ajahdoh phat uvin ama ama in cheh a konin alhamon dingle alhembi dingin thakhat'in ahung kikhom uve. Amin hou chu Teman mi Eliphaz, Shuh mi Bildad chule Naamath mi Zophar ahiuve.
English: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.

tcz: Amahon galla konna Job ahinmu u chun alim amel jong ahethei tapouve. Alung gentheihu nau vetsahna in akap loi loi jengun, aluchung uva huilah a chun leivui atheuvin ahi.
en: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.
text:
JOB 2:12
Thadou: Amahon galla konna Job ahinmu u chun alim amel jong ahethei tapouve. Alung gentheihu nau vetsahna in akap loi loi jengun, aluchung uva huilah a chun leivui atheuvin ahi.
English: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.

tcz: Chuti chun nisagi leh jan sagi tolla atou piuvin, anat genthei hoiset behseh amujeh u chun khatna khatcha jong Job koma thu chengkhat jeng cha seija jong aumpouve; ijeh inem itile anat chu hoise asah behseh jengu ahi.
en: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.
text:
JOB 2:13
Thadou: Chuti chun nisagi leh jan sagi tolla atou piuvin, anat genthei hoiset behseh amujeh u chun khatna khatcha jong Job koma thu chengkhat jeng cha seija jong aumpouve; ijeh inem itile anat chu hoise asah behseh jengu ahi.
English: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.

tcz: Thilsoh hijat nung hin Job akamkan apen nikho agaosap tai.
en: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.
text:
JOB 3:1
Thadou: Thilsoh hijat nung hin Job akamkan apen nikho agaosap tai.
English: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.

tcz: Job in aseijin,
en: Job answered:
text:
JOB 3:2
Thadou: Job in aseijin,
English: Job answered:

tcz: “Kapen nikho le keima mihem a kahung kijil na jan chu chulmangin umhen,
en: “Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, ‘There is a boy conceived.’
text:
JOB 3:3
Thadou: “Kapen nikho le keima mihem a kahung kijil na jan chu chulmangin umhen,
English: “Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, ‘There is a boy conceived.’

tcz: Hiche nikho chu muthim soh jeng hen, Chung Pathen a ding jengin jong mang helhen, chule khovah in salvah hih helhen.
en: Let that day be darkness. Don’t let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.
text:
JOB 3:4
Thadou: Hiche nikho chu muthim soh jeng hen, Chung Pathen a ding jengin jong mang helhen, chule khovah in salvah hih helhen.
English: Let that day be darkness. Don’t let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.

tcz: Hiche nikho chu muthim khojinin kitom mang jeng hen, meivomin khu jeng hen chule muthim chun kichat tijat sah hen.
en: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes the day black terrify it.
text:
JOB 3:5
Thadou: Hiche nikho chu muthim khojinin kitom mang jeng hen, meivomin khu jeng hen chule muthim chun kichat tijat sah hen.
English: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes the day black terrify it.

tcz: Hiche jan chu nikho kisimna a konin kichop mang jeng hen, kum sunga nikho kisimna a avellin kisimtha kit tahih hel hen, lha kisimna holah a jong avellin hung kilang lut hihhen.
en: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.
text:
JOB 3:6
Thadou: Hiche jan chu nikho kisimna a konin kichop mang jeng hen, kum sunga nikho kisimna a avellin kisimtha kit tahih hel hen, lha kisimna holah a jong avellin hung kilang lut hihhen.
English: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.

tcz: Hiche jan chu nao kijil theilouna jan hihen.
en: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.
text:
JOB 3:7
Thadou: Hiche jan chu nao kijil theilouna jan hihen.
English: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.

tcz: Gaosap them Leviathan suthou thei khop a gaosap them hon hiche ni chu gaosap uhen.
en: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.
text:
JOB 3:8
Thadou: Gaosap them Leviathan suthou thei khop a gaosap them hon hiche ni chu gaosap uhen.
English: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.

tcz: Hiche nikho chule jingvalpa jong thim den hen, vahding kinem hen lang ahinlah pannabei hihen lang jingkah khovah jong muhih beh hen.
en: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,
text:
JOB 3:9
Thadou: Hiche nikho chule jingvalpa jong thim den hen, vahding kinem hen lang ahinlah pannabei hihen lang jingkah khovah jong muhih beh hen.
English: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,

tcz: Kanu naobu khah louva anakoi nikho chu gaosap in umhen, leiset gim gentheina jouse mudinga eina pen sah jeh chun.
en: because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.
text:
JOB 3:10
Thadou: Kanu naobu khah louva anakoi nikho chu gaosap in umhen, leiset gim gentheina jouse mudinga eina pen sah jeh chun.
English: because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.

tcz: Ipijeh a athisa a kanapen louham? Kanu naobu a konna kahung doh a chu kana thilou ham?
en: “Why didn’t I die from the womb? Why didn’t I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?
text:
JOB 3:11
Thadou: Ipijeh a athisa a kanapen louham? Kanu naobu a konna kahung doh a chu kana thilou ham?
English: “Why didn’t I die from the womb? Why didn’t I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?

tcz: Ibola kanu phei chunga chu eina kilup sah ham? Ipi bolla kanun anoija eina vah ham?
en: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?
text:
JOB 3:12
Thadou: Ibola kanu phei chunga chu eina kilup sah ham? Ipi bolla kanun anoija eina vah ham?
English: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?

tcz: Kahung pen chun ana thiden leng kei tua hi lungmong tah a kauma kaimutna kicholdo tadinga.
en: For now I should have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,
text:
JOB 3:13
Thadou: Kahung pen chun ana thiden leng kei tua hi lungmong tah a kauma kaimutna kicholdo tadinga.
English: For now I should have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,

tcz: Leiset leng le prime minister oupe u oupe tah tah mangthahsa hotoh kicholdo khoma kium dinga.
en: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;

tcz: Sana haotah tah le ain sungu dangka dimset ho chutoh kichodo khom tading.
en: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver;

tcz: Athisa a peng chapang holeh naosen khovah mukhalou ho banga eina kivui den lou ham?
en: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.
text:
JOB 3:16
Thadou: Athisa a peng chapang holeh naosen khovah mukhalou ho banga eina kivui den lou ham?
English: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.

tcz: Mithisa ho lah a chun miphalou in hahsatna asosah tah lou jeh chun thachol jouse aki choldo tai.
en: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.
text:
JOB 3:17
Thadou: Mithisa ho lah a chun miphalou in hahsatna asosah tah lou jeh chun thachol jouse aki choldo tai.
English: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.

tcz: Thikhol khulla chun sohchang kihen ho jong angah a pangpa sapsetna ajatapouve.
en: There the prisoners are at ease together. They don’t hear the voice of the taskmaster.
text:
JOB 3:18
Thadou: Thikhol khulla chun sohchang kihen ho jong angah a pangpa sapsetna ajatapouve.
English: There the prisoners are at ease together. They don’t hear the voice of the taskmaster.

tcz: Mihao leh migenthei aum khomun chule soh jong apupa a konin a ongthol tai.
en: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.
text:
JOB 3:19
Thadou: Mihao leh migenthei aum khomun chule soh jong apupa a konin a ongthol tai.
English: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.

tcz: Ipi dinga migentheipa hi khovah kimusah a migentheipa hi hinkho kipea ham?
en: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,
text:
JOB 3:20
Thadou: Ipi dinga migentheipa hi khovah kimusah a migentheipa hi hinkho kipea ham?
English: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,

tcz: Thiding angaicha lheh uvin ahinlah thina chu ahung lhung pon, gou kiselguh sangin ngahlel tah in ahol un ahi.
en: who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
text:
JOB 3:21
Thadou: Thiding angaicha lheh uvin ahinlah thina chu ahung lhung pon, gou kiselguh sangin ngahlel tah in ahol un ahi.
English: who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,

tcz: Gentheina jouse athoh chai uva athi teng uleh kipana adimset jiuvin lhankhuh amu teng uleh akipah jiuve.
en: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?
text:
JOB 3:22
Thadou: Gentheina jouse athoh chai uva athi teng uleh kipana adimset jiuvin lhankhuh amu teng uleh akipah jiuve.
English: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?

tcz: Akhonung ding neilou Pathen in hahsatna dimsetna aumkhum ho chu hinkho kipeuva ham?
en: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
text:
JOB 3:23
Thadou: Akhonung ding neilou Pathen in hahsatna dimsetna aumkhum ho chu hinkho kipeuva ham?
English: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?

tcz: Khoisatna ding kanei theipon, kathoh hahsat hohi twi bangin akisung lhai.
en: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.
text:
JOB 3:24
Thadou: Khoisatna ding kanei theipon, kathoh hahsat hohi twi bangin akisung lhai.
English: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.

tcz: Keiman kaki chat pen ipi ham khat kachunga asoh in, hatah a kakichat leh kalung gimna pen ahung lhung tai.
en: For the thing which I fear comes on me, that which I am afraid of comes to me.
text:
JOB 3:25
Thadou: Keiman kaki chat pen ipi ham khat kachunga asoh in, hatah a kakichat leh kalung gimna pen ahung lhung tai.
English: For the thing which I fear comes on me, that which I am afraid of comes to me.

tcz: Lungmonna kanei poi, thipbeh cha umna kanei poi, choldona kanei pon, boina le hahsatna bou ahung ji'e.”
en: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither do I have rest; but trouble comes.”
text:
JOB 3:26
Thadou: Lungmonna kanei poi, thipbeh cha umna kanei poi, choldona kanei pon, boina le hahsatna bou ahung ji'e.”
English: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither do I have rest; but trouble comes.”

tcz: Teman mi Eliphaz chun Job chu adonbut in;
en: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

tcz: Keiman thukhat seijinge, nangaida ding ham? Koiham thusei louva eikoi ding chu?
en: “If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?
text:
JOB 4:2
Thadou: Keiman thukhat seijinge, nangaida ding ham? Koiham thusei louva eikoi ding chu?
English: “If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?

tcz: Phat chesa ho ah nangin mitam tah natil khoujin, alhasam ho nana hatdohsah jin ahi.
en: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.
text:
JOB 4:3
Thadou: Phat chesa ho ah nangin mitam tah natil khoujin, alhasam ho nana hatdohsah jin ahi.
English: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.

tcz: Alhu ding ho jong nangma thusei chun atilkhou jin ahi, akhup kithinghojong na tilkhou ji'e.
en: Your words have supported him who was falling, you have made the feeble knees firm.
text:
JOB 4:4
Thadou: Alhu ding ho jong nangma thusei chun atilkhou jin ahi, akhup kithinghojong na tilkhou ji'e.
English: Your words have supported him who was falling, you have made the feeble knees firm.

tcz: Ahinlah tua genthei nan nahin phah phat in lungthim nalhaso tai. Hiche hahsatnan nahin phah phat in kichat tijatnan nanei tai.
en: But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.
text:
JOB 4:5
Thadou: Ahinlah tua genthei nan nahin phah phat in lungthim nalhaso tai. Hiche hahsatnan nahin phah phat in kichat tijatnan nanei tai.
English: But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.

tcz: Na Pathen ginna chun tahsan detna napeh hilou ham? Nachon phatna chun kinepna napeh hilou ham?
en: Isn’t your piety your confidence? Isn’t the integrity of your ways your hope?
text:
JOB 4:6
Thadou: Na Pathen ginna chun tahsan detna napeh hilou ham? Nachon phatna chun kinepna napeh hilou ham?
English: Isn’t your piety your confidence? Isn’t the integrity of your ways your hope?

tcz: Khongaijin lang chule ngaito temin, themona bei mi hithi ngaiji ham? Itih a milungtheng sel ho kisumang jiem?
en: “Remember, now, who ever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?
text:
JOB 4:7
Thadou: Khongaijin lang chule ngaito temin, themona bei mi hithi ngaiji ham? Itih a milungtheng sel ho kisumang jiem?
English: “Remember, now, who ever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?

tcz: Keithil hetna in vang hahsatna muchi tua kitu ho leh thilse bol hon thakhatna aga akilo cheh diu ahi.
en: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity and sow trouble, reap the same.
text:
JOB 4:8
Thadou: Keithil hetna in vang hahsatna muchi tua kitu ho leh thilse bol hon thakhatna aga akilo cheh diu ahi.
English: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity and sow trouble, reap the same.

tcz: Pathen hu haikhumchun asemgo jiuvin, alung hanna husa ginna chu mang del jiu ahi.
en: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.
text:
JOB 4:9
Thadou: Pathen hu haikhumchun asemgo jiuvin, alung hanna husa ginna chu mang del jiu ahi.
English: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.

tcz: Keipi akitumin chule sangah in mi angih in ahin keipi thahattah hajouse kisubong ding ahi.
en: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
text:
JOB 4:10
Thadou: Keipi akitumin chule sangah in mi angih in ahin keipi thahattah hajouse kisubong ding ahi.
English: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

tcz: Sahing neh ding lhahsam jeh in keipi bahkai hang leiloijin kel athohjin chule keipi bahkai noute jong kithecheh diu ahi.
en: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.
text:
JOB 4:11
Thadou: Sahing neh ding lhahsam jeh in keipi bahkai hang leiloijin kel athohjin chule keipi bahkai noute jong kithecheh diu ahi.
English: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.

tcz: Hiche thutah hi guhthim chan kana benga mao hiuheu vin ei kisei peh e.
en: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.
text:
JOB 4:12
Thadou: Hiche thutah hi guhthim chan kana benga mao hiuheu vin ei kisei peh e.
English: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.

tcz: Mihem aimut lhuh pet tah jan laijin imut sunoh phah in hiche gaova mang thilmuna hi kahenga ahunge.
en: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
text:
JOB 4:13
Thadou: Mihem aimut lhuh pet tah jan laijin imut sunoh phah in hiche gaova mang thilmuna hi kahenga ahunge.
English: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,

tcz: Kichatnan eiphan chule kagu kachang ho akithinge.
en: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.
text:
JOB 4:14
Thadou: Kichatnan eiphan chule kagu kachang ho akithinge.
English: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.

tcz: Thilha hun kamai ahin jap in chule akichaijin katimul ahungkithou sotsotne.
en: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.
text:
JOB 4:15
Thadou: Thilha hun kamai ahin jap in chule akichaijin katimul ahungkithou sotsotne.
English: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.

tcz: Thilha chu adingin ahinla kenla agongso kamuthei pon, agongso kamit teni masang kamaija agongso aum denne. Phat thip laitah chun hitia kisei o khat kajai.
en: It stood still, but I couldn’t discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,
text:
JOB 4:16
Thadou: Thilha chu adingin ahinla kenla agongso kamuthei pon, agongso kamit teni masang kamaija agongso aum denne. Phat thip laitah chun hitia kisei o khat kajai.
English: It stood still, but I couldn’t discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,

tcz: Thithei mihem hi mona beija Pathen anga umtheija, asempa masanga athenga umtheiding hinam?
en: ‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?
text:
JOB 4:17
Thadou: Thithei mihem hi mona beija Pathen anga umtheija, asempa masanga athenga umtheiding hinam?
English: ‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?

tcz: Pathen in avantil ho jeng jong atahsan louva, athupole ho angol naova apho jia ahile,
en: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.
text:
JOB 4:18
Thadou: Pathen in avantil ho jeng jong atahsan louva, athupole ho angol naova apho jia ahile,
English: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.

tcz: Nikhatna kisem mihem hi ichan gei tahsan na anei lhom ding ham? Amaho chu leivuija kisem bailam tah a suhchip thei mitthah tobangbep ahi.
en: How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!
text:
JOB 4:19
Thadou: Nikhatna kisem mihem hi ichan gei tahsan na anei lhom ding ham? Amaho chu leivuija kisem bailam tah a suhchip thei mitthah tobangbep ahi.
English: How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!

tcz: Amaho chu jingkah langleh ahing jiuvin ahinlah nilhah langleh athijiuvin, amelchihna beijin athiji tauve.
en: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.
text:
JOB 4:20
Thadou: Amaho chu jingkah langleh ahing jiuvin ahinlah nilhah langleh athijiuvin, amelchihna beijin athiji tauve.
English: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.

tcz: Aponbuh henna akibo lhuh teng leh apon buh u alhujin chule hetna lhasam in athiden ji tauve.
en: Isn’t their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.’
text:
JOB 4:21
Thadou: Aponbuh henna akibo lhuh teng leh apon buh u alhujin chule hetna lhasam in athiden ji tauve.
English: Isn’t their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.’

tcz: Na kithopi ding kou temin mikhat beh in nahin donbut na dem? Vantil ho koipen in nahin kithopi ding ham?
en: “Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
text:
JOB 5:1
Thadou: Na kithopi ding kou temin mikhat beh in nahin donbut na dem? Vantil ho koipen in nahin kithopi ding ham?
English: “Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

tcz: Tahbeh in lung hanna hin mingol asuhmang jia chule thangsetna in chihna neilou ho asumang ji'e.
en: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.
text:
JOB 5:2
Thadou: Tahbeh in lung hanna hin mingol asuhmang jia chule thangsetna in chihna neilou ho asumang ji'e.
English: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.

tcz: Keiman mingol ho chomkhat kahsung alolhin nao kamui ahinla vangset na chun hetman louvin alhunkhum jitai.
en: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
text:
JOB 5:3
Thadou: Keiman mingol ho chomkhat kahsung alolhin nao kamui ahinla vangset na chun hetman louvin alhunkhum jitai.
English: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

tcz: Achateo jong ajong ajellin gamsa chonin achonun amaho dingin panpina agamlan ahi, ahuhdoh diu umlouvin thutanna munna amehgoi jiuve.
en: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,
text:
JOB 5:4
Thadou: Achateo jong ajong ajellin gamsa chonin achonun amaho dingin panpina agamlan ahi, ahuhdoh diu umlouvin thutanna munna amehgoi jiuve.
English: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,

tcz: Achang chu lingleh khauva akium jeng vang'in agilkel ten avallhum peh un, agou chu adangchah ten hai hot hot in adel uve.
en: whose harvest the hungry eat up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.
text:
JOB 5:5
Thadou: Achang chu lingleh khauva akium jeng vang'in agilkel ten avallhum peh un, agou chu adangchah ten hai hot hot in adel uve.
English: whose harvest the hungry eat up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.

tcz: Thilse hi leivui lah a konna hungput doh ahipoi chule hahsatna hi leisetna konna hung dondoh ahipoi.
en: For affliction doesn’t come out of the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;

tcz: Meilah a konna meisi chunglanga lengtou dinga gotsa aum banga mihem tehi ahahsa ding monga penga ahi.
en: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.
text:
JOB 5:7
Thadou: Meilah a konna meisi chunglanga lengtou dinga gotsa aum banga mihem tehi ahahsa ding monga penga ahi.
English: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

tcz: Keihi nang chu hileng Pathen koma cheng ting chule kachung chang thu ama koma kase lhah ding ahi.
en: “But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,
text:
JOB 5:8
Thadou: Keihi nang chu hileng Pathen koma cheng ting chule kachung chang thu ama koma kase lhah ding ahi.
English: “But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,

tcz: Aman thil oupe tah hetdoh jou hoi hilou ajat sim joulou thil kidang aboldoh e.
en: who does great things that can’t be fathomed, marvelous things without number;

tcz: Aman leiset chunga go ajuh sah jin, chule loulaija jong twi alonsah soh keije.
en: who gives rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;

tcz: Aman mivaichate khantouna apen chule genthei hesoh thohte ahuhdoh ji'e.
en: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.
text:
JOB 5:11
Thadou: Aman mivaichate khantouna apen chule genthei hesoh thohte ahuhdoh ji'e.
English: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.

tcz: Athil gonu asuh nohphah peh in, hijeh chun akhut uva atoh jouseu amolso joulou diu ahi.
en: He frustrates the plans of the crafty, so that their hands can’t perform their enterprise.
text:
JOB 5:12
Thadou: Athil gonu asuh nohphah peh in, hijeh chun akhut uva atoh jouseu amolso joulou diu ahi.
English: He frustrates the plans of the crafty, so that their hands can’t perform their enterprise.

tcz: Miching ho chu aki chihsah nauva amang jin hijeh chun aduha thuh nauva athil gonnu asuhbei pehji tai.
en: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.
text:
JOB 5:13
Thadou: Miching ho chu aki chihsah nauva amang jin hijeh chun aduha thuh nauva athil gonnu asuhbei pehji tai.
English: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.

tcz: Amahon sun laijin muthim atoh khauvin sunkim laijin amaho chu janlai bangin aki mai le leuve.
en: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.
text:
JOB 5:14
Thadou: Amahon sun laijin muthim atoh khauvin sunkim laijin amaho chu janlai bangin aki mai le leuve.
English: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.

tcz: Mikam hatte a konin mi vaichate ahuhdoh jin chule mithahat ten atuhchah kheh hou jong amaho a konin ahuhdoh ji'e.
en: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.
text:
JOB 5:15
Thadou: Mikam hatte a konin mi vaichate ahuhdoh jin chule mithahat ten atuhchah kheh hou jong amaho a konin ahuhdoh ji'e.
English: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.

tcz: Chule hiche ho a chun achaina leh mivaichan kinepna aneiyin, chule mihahem te kam jong ahuhbit jin ahi.
en: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.
text:
JOB 5:16
Thadou: Chule hiche ho a chun achaina leh mivaichan kinepna aneiyin, chule mihahem te kam jong ahuhbit jin ahi.
English: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.

tcz: Ahinla Pathen in asuhdih ho kipana khu ngaito temin, nachonset tengleh Hatchungung pan nahilna khu don louvin koi hih in.
en: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.
text:
JOB 5:17
Thadou: Ahinla Pathen in asuhdih ho kipana khu ngaito temin, nachonset tengleh Hatchungung pan nahilna khu don louvin koi hih in.
English: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

tcz: Aman amavo jin chule boljong aboldam jin aman ajep jin ahinla akhut in asudam kitjin ahi.
en: For he wounds and binds up. He injures and his hands make whole.
text:
JOB 5:18
Thadou: Aman amavo jin chule boljong aboldam jin aman ajep jin ahinla akhut in asudam kitjin ahi.
English: For he wounds and binds up. He injures and his hands make whole.

tcz: Vangsetna gupma konin nahuhdoh intin asagi veina teng jongleh thilse akonin nahoi doh inte.
en: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil will touch you.
text:
JOB 5:19
Thadou: Vangsetna gupma konin nahuhdoh intin asagi veina teng jongleh thilse akonin nahoi doh inte.
English: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil will touch you.

tcz: Kellhah lai jongle thina akonin nahuhdoh intin gallai jongleh chemjama konin nahuh doh inte.
en: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.
text:
JOB 5:20
Thadou: Kellhah lai jongle thina akonin nahuhdoh intin gallai jongleh chemjama konin nahuh doh inte.
English: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.

tcz: Misuminse nom te akonin hung hoidoh in natin chule manthahna ahung lhun teng kicha tapon nate.
en: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither will you be afraid of destruction when it comes.
text:
JOB 5:21
Thadou: Misuminse nom te akonin hung hoidoh in natin chule manthahna ahung lhun teng kicha tapon nate.
English: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither will you be afraid of destruction when it comes.

tcz: Manthah nale kel alhah teng nangin nanuisat ding gamlah a gamsa jouse nagin louding ahitai.
en: You will laugh at destruction and famine, neither will you be afraid of the animals of the earth.
text:
JOB 5:22
Thadou: Manthah nale kel alhah teng nangin nanuisat ding gamlah a gamsa jouse nagin louding ahitai.
English: You will laugh at destruction and famine, neither will you be afraid of the animals of the earth.

tcz: Nangma gam lah a songho toh lungmong tah a naum khoma chule gamlah a gamsa ho toh lungmonga nalhat khom diu ahitai.
en: For you will be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field will be at peace with you.
text:
JOB 5:23
Thadou: Nangma gam lah a songho toh lungmong tah a naum khoma chule gamlah a gamsa ho toh lungmonga nalhat khom diu ahitai.
English: For you will be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field will be at peace with you.

tcz: Nachenna nain abitne ti nakihetna, nanei nagou ho nagavet teng imacha akiholmo umlou ding ahi.
en: You will know that your tent is in peace. You will visit your fold, and will miss nothing.
text:
JOB 5:24
Thadou: Nachenna nain abitne ti nakihetna, nanei nagou ho nagavet teng imacha akiholmo umlou ding ahi.
English: You will know that your tent is in peace. You will visit your fold, and will miss nothing.

tcz: Nangin chate tamtah neijin natin, nason nachilhahte hampa banga hung tam diu ahi.
en: You will know also that your offspring will be great, your offspring as the grass of the earth.
text:
JOB 5:25
Thadou: Nangin chate tamtah neijin natin, nason nachilhahte hampa banga hung tam diu ahi.
English: You will know also that your offspring will be great, your offspring as the grass of the earth.

tcz: Nateh teng lhankhuh hin jonin natin, aphat cha changpholla changpal kichom khom nahung bah ding ahi.
en: You will come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.
text:
JOB 5:26
Thadou: Nateh teng lhankhuh hin jonin natin, aphat cha changpholla changpal kichom khom nahung bah ding ahi.
English: You will come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.

tcz: Keihon hinkho hi kakhol uvin, chule hichehi dih din kamu doh uve, kahilna hi ngaijin chule nangma tah a dingin mangchan.
en: Behold, we have researched it. It is so. Hear it, and know it for your good.”
text:
JOB 5:27
Thadou: Keihon hinkho hi kakhol uvin, chule hichehi dih din kamu doh uve, kahilna hi ngaijin chule nangma tah a dingin mangchan.
English: Behold, we have researched it. It is so. Hear it, and know it for your good.”

tcz: Hichun Job apaodoh kit in:
en: Then Job answered,
text:
JOB 6:1
Thadou: Hichun Job apaodoh kit in:
English: Then Job answered,

tcz: Kagenthei naho hi tedoh thei hihen lang ka natna hi kilep toh thei henlang hileh,
en: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
text:
JOB 6:2
Thadou: Kagenthei naho hi tedoh thei hihen lang ka natna hi kilep toh thei henlang hileh,
English: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!

tcz: Twikhanglen'a neldi umjat sangin gih jonte, hiche ho jeh a chu khongai man louhella kaseidoh ji ahi.
en: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore my words have been rash.
text:
JOB 6:3
Thadou: Twikhanglen'a neldi umjat sangin gih jonte, hiche ho jeh a chu khongai man louhella kaseidoh ji ahi.
English: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore my words have been rash.

tcz: Hat Chungungpa thal hanging eikap lhuh tah jeh chun athal gu chun kalhagao asukhan, Pathenna kon tijatna ho chu keidou din ahung kigoltoh tauve.
en: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.
text:
JOB 6:4
Thadou: Hat Chungungpa thal hanging eikap lhuh tah jeh chun athal gu chun kalhagao asukhan, Pathenna kon tijatna ho chu keidou din ahung kigoltoh tauve.
English: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.

tcz: Kalunglhai louna thu seitheina tha kanei hilou ham? Gamlah sangan chun nehding hampa akimu jilou teng penglouva umjia chule bongchal ten jong neh ding aneilou teng buji hilou ham?
en: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?
text:
JOB 6:5
Thadou: Kalunglhai louna thu seitheina tha kanei hilou ham? Gamlah sangan chun nehding hampa akimu jilou teng penglouva umjia chule bongchal ten jong neh ding aneilou teng buji hilou ham?
English: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?

tcz: Chiso louna anneh chunga chu mihon alung lhailou nao aseiji louvu ham? A-alna bei ahtwi kang podal khu kon adu ding ham?
en: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
text:
JOB 6:6
Thadou: Chiso louna anneh chunga chu mihon alung lhailou nao aseiji louvu ham? A-alna bei ahtwi kang podal khu kon adu ding ham?
English: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

tcz: Kavet jiteng ka-an duna abei jitai, neh dinga kangaito najouse akikhah tansoh jitai.
en: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.
text:
JOB 6:7
Thadou: Kavet jiteng ka-an duna abei jitai, neh dinga kangaito najouse akikhah tansoh jitai.
English: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.

tcz: Oh, keiman kadei khat kaki thum thei ding hihen, Pathen chun kadei chu eipeh ding hileh,
en: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,
text:
JOB 6:8
Thadou: Oh, keiman kadei khat kaki thum thei ding hihen, Pathen chun kadei chu eipeh ding hileh,
English: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,

tcz: Aman eisuh chip jeng ding kadeije, akhut ahin lhandoh a chule eitha jeng ding kadeije
en: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
text:
JOB 6:9
Thadou: Aman eisuh chip jeng ding kadeije, akhut ahin lhandoh a chule eitha jeng ding kadeije
English: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

tcz: Natgim genthei thoh'a kimusetna ho a konna hiche beh a hi lung monna kaneiding ahi. Athengpa thusei nahsahmon kabol khapoi.
en: Let it still be my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
text:
JOB 6:10
Thadou: Natgim genthei thoh'a kimusetna ho a konna hiche beh a hi lung monna kaneiding ahi. Athengpa thusei nahsahmon kabol khapoi.
English: Let it still be my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

tcz: Ahinlah athoh jou nading thahat kaneipoi, keiman hinpi ding imacha kaneipoi.
en: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?
text:
JOB 6:11
Thadou: Ahinlah athoh jou nading thahat kaneipoi, keiman hinpi ding imacha kaneipoi.
English: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?

tcz: Songthahatna chu nei kahim? Katahsa hi sum eng kisem ham?
en: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of bronze?
text:
JOB 6:12
Thadou: Songthahatna chu nei kahim? Katahsa hi sum eng kisem ham?
English: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of bronze?

tcz: Ahipoi keima ahin lolhinnaphat gomkom neilou kithopi beihel kahi.
en: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, that wisdom is driven away from me?
text:
JOB 6:13
Thadou: Ahipoi keima ahin lolhinnaphat gomkom neilou kithopi beihel kahi.
English: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, that wisdom is driven away from me?

tcz: Agol apai lhasam khat dinga lungsetna nei mi hiding ahinla nangin Hatchungungpa kicha louvin themmo neichanne.
en: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
text:
JOB 6:14
Thadou: Agol apai lhasam khat dinga lungsetna nei mi hiding ahinla nangin Hatchungungpa kicha louvin themmo neichanne.
English: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

tcz: Kasopi teho aphat phat cha long ji vadung neocha banga tahsan theilou, khaltwi vadung neocha akam dima long tobang nahiu naphot chenu ahi.
en: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;

tcz: Buhbang lhang le buhbang twi kikhol khom chu,
en: which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.
text:
JOB 6:16
Thadou: Buhbang lhang le buhbang twi kikhol khom chu,
English: which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.

tcz: Kholum phat ahung lhun tengleh twi chua amangjin, vadung neucha chu asat jeh chun amang jitai.
en: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
text:
JOB 6:17
Thadou: Kholum phat ahung lhun tengleh twi chua amangjin, vadung neucha chu asat jeh chun amang jitai.
English: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

tcz: Kholjin miho chu holdoh kitna ding in akihei doh jiuvin, ahin donding aum loujeh chun athiji tauve.
en: The caravans that travel beside them turn away. They go up into the waste, and perish.
text:
JOB 6:18
Thadou: Kholjin miho chu holdoh kitna ding in akihei doh jiuvin, ahin donding aum loujeh chun athiji tauve.
English: The caravans that travel beside them turn away. They go up into the waste, and perish.

tcz: Tema a hung kholjin miho chun twi ahol jiuvin, Sheba a hung kholjin miho chun neiding akinem uve.
en: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.
text:
JOB 6:19
Thadou: Tema a hung kholjin miho chun twi ahol jiuvin, Sheba a hung kholjin miho chun neiding akinem uve.
English: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.

tcz: Akinep nao chu asim jiuvin ahinlah alunglhai jipouve, ahung lhun tengleh akinep nao akisudong jitauve.
en: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.
text:
JOB 6:20
Thadou: Akinep nao chu asim jiuvin ahinlah alunglhai jipouve, ahung lhun tengleh akinep nao akisudong jitauve.
English: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.

tcz: Nanghon jong kithopina neipe pouve, kavang setna namuvin chule naki chauve.
en: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.
text:
JOB 6:21
Thadou: Nanghon jong kithopina neipe pouve, kavang setna namuvin chule naki chauve.
English: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.

tcz: Ahinlah ipijeh ham? Keiman thilpeh khattou kathum khah em? Keiman nanei ikhat tou keiding tuma kathum khah em?
en: Did I ever say, ‘Give to me’? or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance’?
text:
JOB 6:22
Thadou: Ahinlah ipijeh ham? Keiman thilpeh khattou kathum khah em? Keiman nanei ikhat tou keiding tuma kathum khah em?
English: Did I ever say, ‘Give to me’? or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance’?

tcz: Melma pa a konin nei huhdoh un tia kasei khah a, ahilouleh lungsetna neilou miho a konin nei huhdoh un tia kaseikhah em?
en: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand’? or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors’?
text:
JOB 6:23
Thadou: Melma pa a konin nei huhdoh un tia kasei khah a, ahilouleh lungsetna neilou miho a konin nei huhdoh un tia kaseikhah em?
English: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand’? or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors’?

tcz: Neihillin, chutilehthipbeh in um inge, ipi kabol khel um'em neivetsah in?
en: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand my error.
text:
JOB 6:24
Thadou: Neihillin, chutilehthipbeh in um inge, ipi kabol khel um'em neivetsah in?
English: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand my error.

tcz: Lungtheng sella kiseidoh thucheng hi itobanga thahat hitam? Ahin neidem nao ijat aphah hitam?
en: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?
text:
JOB 6:25
Thadou: Lungtheng sella kiseidoh thucheng hi itobanga thahat hitam? Ahin neidem nao ijat aphah hitam?
English: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?

tcz: Kalung natna kakana ija naselou tenguleh nathusei houhin mi jouvinte natiuvem?
en: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?
text:
JOB 6:26
Thadou: Kalung natna kakana ija naselou tenguleh nathusei houhin mi jouvinte natiuvem?
English: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?

tcz: Chagate ahiloule nagol napaite jeng jong soh in naso jiuve.
en: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.
text:
JOB 6:27
Thadou: Chagate ahiloule nagol napaite jeng jong soh in naso jiuve.
English: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.

tcz: Neihin vetan, namai chang tah a kajou ding ham?
en: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I will not lie to your face.
text:
JOB 6:28
Thadou: Neihin vetan, namai chang tah a kajou ding ham?
English: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I will not lie to your face.

tcz: Kachonsetna hi dih nante tin gelda tauvin, ijeh inem itile keiman bolkhel kaneipoi.
en: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.
text:
JOB 6:29
Thadou: Kachonsetna hi dih nante tin gelda tauvin, ijeh inem itile keiman bolkhel kaneipoi.
English: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.

tcz: Thujou seidinga nei gelluvem? Aphale ase hekhen thei lou ding kahim?
en: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?
text:
JOB 6:30
Thadou: Thujou seidinga nei gelluvem? Aphale ase hekhen thei lou ding kahim?
English: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?

tcz: Mihem jouse hinkho hi hahsatna toh kidel jing hilou ham? Ihinkho uhi kitha lah khut tobang hilou ham?
en: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?
text:
JOB 7:1
Thadou: Mihem jouse hinkho hi hahsatna toh kidel jing hilou ham? Ihinkho uhi kitha lah khut tobang hilou ham?
English: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?

tcz: Liim ngaicha aum natong mi tobang ahin, soh atohna man ngah tobang ahi.
en: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,
text:
JOB 7:2
Thadou: Liim ngaicha aum natong mi tobang ahin, soh atohna man ngah tobang ahi.
English: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,

tcz: Keima jong lha phabep sunga chu phatchomna bei natoh eikipen ahi, lunggel gentheina dimset in jankho sot noijah genthei kathoh e.
en: so I am made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.
text:
JOB 7:3
Thadou: Keima jong lha phabep sunga chu phatchomna bei natoh eikipen ahi, lunggel gentheina dimset in jankho sot noijah genthei kathoh e.
English: so I am made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.

tcz: Jalkhun chungah kalumin, itih tah le jingkah ahitadem tin kagel jin, ahinlah jan in eisu chol in khovah kahsen kaki pehle le jin ahi.
en: When I lie down, I say, ‘When will I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
text:
JOB 7:4
Thadou: Jalkhun chungah kalumin, itih tah le jingkah ahitadem tin kagel jin, ahinlah jan in eisu chol in khovah kahsen kaki pehle le jin ahi.
English: When I lie down, I say, ‘When will I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.

tcz: Kati chungla than leh akhih in atom dimin ka vun jong apohkeh gamin anai along longe.
en: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.
text:
JOB 7:5
Thadou: Kati chungla than leh akhih in atom dimin ka vun jong apohkeh gamin anai along longe.
English: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.

tcz: Ka nikho ho jong pon khong ho patphei kilham sangin ging jon, kinepna beijin akichai ji'e.
en: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
text:
JOB 7:6
Thadou: Ka nikho ho jong pon khong ho patphei kilham sangin ging jon, kinepna beijin akichai ji'e.
English: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.

tcz: O Pathen, kahin kho hi hai khat bep bou ahi ti nei geldoh peh in, chule keiman kipana hi kanei kit lou hel ding ahi.
en: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye will no more see good.
text:
JOB 7:7
Thadou: O Pathen, kahin kho hi hai khat bep bou ahi ti nei geldoh peh in, chule keiman kipana hi kanei kit lou hel ding ahi.
English: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye will no more see good.

tcz: Nangin tua hi neimu ahin, ahinlah nei musot pon nate, nangin neiven natin ahinlah keima ana chemang tange.
en: The eye of him who sees me will see me no more. Your eyes will be on me, but I will not be.
text:
JOB 7:8
Thadou: Nangin tua hi neimu ahin, ahinlah nei musot pon nate, nangin neiven natin ahinlah keima ana chemang tange.
English: The eye of him who sees me will see me no more. Your eyes will be on me, but I will not be.

tcz: Meilhang akithecheh a aman hel bangin, athiho khu hung kile kit tapou vinte.
en: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol will come up no more.
text:
JOB 7:9
Thadou: Meilhang akithecheh a aman hel bangin, athiho khu hung kile kit tapou vinte.
English: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol will come up no more.

tcz: Amaho chu ainuva patna tonsotna mukit tah lou dinga chemang ahitauve.
en: He will return no more to his house, neither will his place know him any more.
text:
JOB 7:10
Thadou: Amaho chu ainuva patna tonsotna mukit tah lou dinga chemang ahitauve.
English: He will return no more to his house, neither will his place know him any more.

tcz: Keima thusei louvin kaum theipoi, kalung genthei naho kasei doh a ka lhagao genthei jeh a kiphin ding kahi.
en: “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
text:
JOB 7:11
Thadou: Keima thusei louvin kaum theipoi, kalung genthei naho kasei doh a ka lhagao genthei jeh a kiphin ding kahi.
English: “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

tcz: Keima hi twikhanglen'a kichat chat um ganhing len ahilouleh gullui kahia nahonbit nanoija chu neikoi jeng ding ham?
en: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
text:
JOB 7:12
